note: BOUNDED, NOT UNBOUNDED: verdict holds only for <= 3 single-cycle bit-flip faults (gate outputs and flop Q) within 6 cycles on this synthesized netlist. It says nothing about more faults, longer runs, other fault types (stuck-at, multi-bit/spatial, clock/voltage effects), or physical feasibility. Toy design; modelled faults.

explanation.summary: MINIMUM ATTACK COST = 3 faults (`$flatten\c0.$abc$251$new_n16_`@1, `$flatten\c1.$abc$251$new_n15_`@1, `$flatten\c2.$abc$251$new_n15_`@1). No single net decides, but the faults found hit independent redundant copies; the attacker needs 3 coordinated single-cycle flips (spanning 1 distinct cycle(s)).
explanation.fix_pattern: Raise the cost above the attacker's fault budget: add another independent copy (so quorum needs >3), keep every copy's result in its own disjoint output bits, and add a sticky alarm on any disagreement. Re-run the tool at k=3.
